_why: One budget per model, written once, so a control cell and the treatment
cell it is compared against cannot drift apart. They did: BFS control ran
at token_budget 16384 / max_actions 200 while its treatment ran at 8192 /
40, and 8% of treatment episodes were cut off at an action ceiling the
control never reached. The measured drop carried that difference inside it
and the control had to be re-run.
Flags typed at the shell are what allowed it. Cells are declared here
instead, and `scripts/run_exam_cell.py` refuses to start one whose budget
differs from the control it names.

bfs._serving: llama.cpp only — LM Studio returns logprobs: null and the scored sampler silently degrades to an unscored frontier walk
bfs._local_serving_why: llama.cpp only, Q8_0: the search ranks candidates by cumulative token log-probability, which LM Studio's completion endpoint does not return.

goedel._serving: needs >= 16384 context: prompt + max_tokens 4096 exceeds 8192 on longer rows and the server answers 400
goedel._declared_why: Declared 2026-09-04 for the replay of 14 truncated treatment episodes. Both arms record prompt_style=goedel_v2 on every episode written after the field existed (362 treatment, 3 control; older episodes predate it), and the cell has only ever been served from a local llama.cpp at Q8_0. The parity and serving gates read declarations, not history, so the replay refused until both were said out loud.

luna._model: openai/gpt-5.6-luna through OpenRouter, the same transport and dialect as grok
luna._why_not_codex:
This cell used to be driven through `codex exec`, and that was not a fair reading of the model -- it was not even a reading of the model alone. `codex exec` is an agent, it was called with cwd unset so it inherited the runner's working directory, and `--sandbox read-only` lets an agent read files there. The repository holds the answers: release535_playable.jsonl carries gt_proof_body for all 535 rows and seeds_all100.jsonl carries a proof for every one of the 100 seeds.

It read them. Normalising whitespace and comments, 124 of the 470 treatment proofs longer than 150 characters match the released ground truth exactly, including a 52-line, 1,960-character dihedral-group argument reproduced lemma for lemma. Nothing about the old cell's 100.0/99.6/99.3 was a measurement of proving ability, and every claim that rested on it -- the ceiling reference, the near-zero LPG floor -- rested on nothing.

An HTTP endpoint has no filesystem to read, so the contamination cannot recur here by construction. Matching grok's player, dialect and budget also removes the second asymmetry: the old cell reported no usage, so the 8192 budget never bound it, and it took no assistant turn. The old episodes are kept under *_contaminated_codex.
luna._reasoning_headroom_why: Measured on three rows of varying difficulty: 4,293 / 198 / 271 reasoning tokens, each finishing on its own with an extractable block. 8192 clears the largest with room.
luna._first_party_why: OpenAI's model over OpenRouter's passthrough to OpenAI; no third-party host is involved.

pythagoras._model: Pythagoras-Prover-4B-Q8_0.gguf — a third dedicated prover, and the smallest in the panel at 4B
pythagoras._serving:
FriendliAI dedicated endpoint, 1x H100, serving Pythagoras-Prover-4B at its native bf16 with online quantization off -- the panel's floor is eight bits and the model card's torch_dtype is bfloat16, so serving it unquantised is both inside the rule and closest to what the authors released. Speculative decoding and the n-gram accelerator are off: they are meant to be output-equivalent, but under temperature sampling that equivalence is an implementation property, not a guarantee, and this is a measurement run. The reasoning parser is off too -- this model has no reasoning channel, it writes its plan as ordinary content, and a parser that lifted the plan into `reasoning_content` would collide with the fence-based split this cell already does. Measured at 193 tok/s, about 50s per episode.

The 218 local Q8_0 control episodes are archived rather than continued: a serving stack is part of a cell, and half a control arm from llama.cpp on Apple silicon does not belong beside half from an H100. Both arms will run here.
pythagoras._prefill_why: Off, and for the same reason as leanstral's. The official prompt asks for a detailed proof plan *before* the Lean; a prefill that opens the turn with the code fence leaves nowhere to write it. Measured: the model skips the plan and emits `have h_main ... := by have h1 ... := by have h2 ...`, pushing the same goal into itself until the window ends, with `-- this is a standard result in group theory` for a proof. The fence also arrives twice once the server echoes the prefill, and the extractor reads no code at all. The prefill is Goedel's prescription and does not transfer.
pythagoras._official_settings:
The repo's `evaluation/utils.py` uses the Goedel-V2 prompt verbatim -- 'provide a detailed proof plan' before the Lean -- at temperature 1.0 and top_p 0.95, which the cell matches. (The HF card's generation_config.json instead carries 0.6 / top_k 20; the evaluation script is the more specific source and wins.) Their max_tokens of 8192 is matched too. The card states four times that the model works *without inference-time self-correction*, and its usage example calls generate() once with max_new_tokens=8192: one plan plus one proof is what 8192 was sized for.

Measured against 4096 on a 20-row mixed probe (10 ProofNet, 10 miniF2F), pass@1, same seeds, same everything else. Accuracy is identical -- 8 solved out of 20 under both, and the same 8 rows; no row flips. Both also deliver a candidate to Lean exactly 24 times (16 rejected + 8 solved). What differs is how many attempts that costs: 45 at 4096 against 35 at 8192. The 10 extra attempts at 4096 are all waste -- attempts yielding no extractable Lean rise from 10 to 21 (29% -> 47%) and truncation from 5% to 11%, because the plan the official prompt demands does not fit alongside the proof in a 4096 slice. Those attempts are not revisions from a Lean diagnostic; they are retries after the model's own truncated output. 8192 is chosen for that, not for accuracy.
pythagoras._attempts_why: max_attempts stays at 4, the same nominal ceiling every whole-proof cell gets. No cell is granted a number of attempts; the budget decides. Measured attempts per episode: leanstral 3.0 (161 proof tokens per attempt), goedel 3.4 (1169), pythagoras 1.8 at 8192 and 2.2 at 4096. Leanstral reaches four attempts because its proofs are short, not because it was given more room, and pythagoras's 2.2 at 4096 is not more chances than its 1.8 at 8192 -- the extra attempts are the misfires counted above. Holding tokens rather than attempts is the same invariant that lets a 40-action tactic search be compared with a revision loop at all.
pythagoras._plan_outside_budget_why:
The official prompt asks for a detailed proof plan before the Lean, and that plan is deliberation emitted as ordinary content rather than through a reasoning channel. Measured on the first 34 control episodes: 81% of a *successful* attempt's tokens were the plan (about 1,379 per attempt, ~2,620 of the 8,192-token episode budget at 1.9 attempts), against a goedel cell that skips the plan by prefill and spends its whole budget on Lean. Charging it meant the channel a model happens to think in decided how much proof it was allowed to write, which is the one thing the budget exists to hold fixed. Only the fenced proof is charged now.

Only this cell sets it. A prefilled cell opens the fence in the prompt and LM Studio returns the continuation alone, so its reply carries a closing fence and no opening one; splitting there would put nearly the whole proof on the plan side and the budget would stop binding altogether.

reasoning_headroom is 2048 for the same reason it is nonzero on the reasoning SLMs: the plan is counted inside max_tokens by the endpoint even though it is now outside the budget, so the *request* has to carry room for it. 2048 is ~1.5x the measured plan.
pythagoras._local_alternative: llama.cpp with models/Pythagoras-Prover-4B-Q8_0.gguf on port 8081, ~160s per episode. That is what the archived pythagoras_control_local_q8 rows were run on.
pythagoras._first_party_why: FriendliAI dedicated endpoint we configure ourselves: online quantisation off, native bf16.

grok._budget_binds: unlike luna: OpenRouter is OpenAI-compatible and reports usage.completion_tokens, so the 8192 budget actually binds and this cell's absolute score is comparable, not just its drop
grok._why_dialect: goedel_v1 is plain instruct English -- 'complete the following Lean 4 code, return one fenced block' -- with no prover-specific scaffold. The generic template additionally shows the natural-language statement, which no prover in the panel receives; giving it to the general models alone would put an information asymmetry inside the main comparison.
grok._content_allowance: xAI caps max_tokens against the visible answer and lets thinking run past it, so 4096 *is* the proof allowance. `reasoning.max_tokens` is ignored here (64 requested, 289 spent) and `reasoning.enabled=false` is refused.
grok._reasoning_headroom_why: Measured through OpenRouter, which is the interface this cell uses. The former 0 was carried over from the direct xAI API, where max_tokens caps the visible answer and thinking sits outside it; through OpenRouter the reasoning is counted inside the same cap. At max_tokens 4096 a ProofNet row came back with 3,349 of those tokens spent on reasoning and roughly 750 left for Lean -- it fit, but only just, and the reasoning SLMs showed what happens when it does not: a reply truncated mid-thought carries no content at all and is filed as `no_code`. Observed reasoning across three rows of varying difficulty is 1,371 / 2,418 / 3,769, every one finishing on its own; 8192 clears the largest with room to spare. The 8192 proof budget beside it is unchanged.
grok._withdrawn: Withdrawn for cost. The control arm is complete and verified -- 58.0% on \minif and 54.0% on \proofb over 300 episodes, 115 claimed proofs re-checked against their own statements with none failing -- and is kept under grok_control as a record. The treatment arm is not run: at $6.00 per million output tokens and 27,126 tokens an episode it costs about $261, which is more than the rest of the panel's hosted cells put together, and a pass@1 variant at $87 would have put one row of the table on a different criterion from every other row. The frontier group keeps three models with both arms.

nemotron._cap: Crusoe ignores the cap (512 requested, 1091 spent); headroom only
nemotron._reasoning_headroom_why: Measured, not assumed. On a hard ProofNet row under the cell's own goedel_v1 prompt this model spends 18,932 reasoning tokens before it writes anything, finishing on its own. The former 8192 cut it off mid-thought: the reply came back with finish_reason=length, zero characters of content, and the episode was filed as `no_code` -- the model failing to produce Lean, when in fact it never got to write any. Across the first 44 episodes of the four-cell control that was 37% of all attempts. 24,576 is the measured figure with headroom to spare; easy miniF2F rows cost a fraction of it and are unaffected.

leanstral._model: labs-leanstral-1-5 (mistralai/Leanstral-1.5-119B-A6B, Apache-2.0) -- MoE 119B/6.5B active. Reports usage and emits no reasoning channel, so the budget binds exactly: an open-weight ceiling that needs no asterisk.
leanstral._endpoint: https://api.mistral.ai/v1 -- public preview, retirement announced for 2026-09-30. Weights remain under Apache-2.0.
leanstral._sampling: Mistral refuses temperature 0 unless top_p is 1; the cell's 1.0/0.95 is unaffected.
leanstral._official_settings: The model card asks for temperature 1.0 and reasoning effort 'high' for complex prompts. Run without it the model answers in ~140 tokens and truncates mid-`calc`; with it, 811 tokens and a finished proof. Switching it on also changes the response schema -- `content` becomes a list of typed blocks rather than a string -- which the transport now handles.
leanstral._protocol_note: Leanstral is released as a Lean *code agent*, meant to be driven through lean-lsp-mcp over long horizons. We measure it in the same single-shot whole-proof protocol as the rest of the panel, which is the comparison this paper is making; its published miniF2F figure is not one we attempt to reproduce.
leanstral._prefill_why: Off, and not by preference. With the assistant turn opened, Mistral returns [text, thinking, text] instead of [thinking, text] -- the model reasons inside the code fence, never closes it, and the attempt hits the request ceiling and returns `unexpected end of input`. Every episode so configured burned 12296 tokens on one truncated attempt. The prefill saves budget; reasoning effort decides whether a proof finishes, so the prefill is the one that gives way.
leanstral._generate_timeout_why: The default is lean_timeout*2 = 360s, and this cell hit it exactly: 14 control episodes came back after 360.x seconds with no attempts, recorded as `generator_empty`, and three consecutive ones aborted the cell twice. Mistral with reasoning effort high routinely spends longer than that on a ProofNet row -- the measured episodes that did finish took 500-880s. 900 clears the observed range. The wait costs nothing that is measured: the proof budget is tokens, not seconds.
leanstral._first_party_why: Mistral serving Mistral's own model; there is no second host to choose between.
leanstral._api_key_env_why: Renamed 2026-09-04 from MISTRAL_API: the transport falls back to OPENROUTER_API_KEY when the named variable is unset, so a key saved under the conventional name produced a 401 from Mistral rather than a missing-key error.

muse._arch: dense 30B, Meta Superintelligence Labs, distilled from Muse Spark
muse._quantisation: bf16; no fp8 endpoint exists, and bf16 is above the eight-bit floor
muse._cap: DeepInfra honours reasoning.max_tokens for this model -- 256 requested, 216 spent -- and it is the only cell in the panel where the cap binds. Honouring is a property of the model-and-serving pair: the same provider ignores the field for qwen3.6.
muse._reasoning_headroom_why: Measured, not assumed. On a hard ProofNet row under the cell's own goedel_v1 prompt this model spends 11,498 reasoning tokens before it writes anything, finishing on its own. The former 8192 cut it off mid-thought: the reply came back with finish_reason=length, zero characters of content, and the episode was filed as `no_code` -- the model failing to produce Lean, when in fact it never got to write any. Across the first 44 episodes of the four-cell control that was 37% of all attempts. 16,384 is the measured figure with headroom to spare; easy miniF2F rows cost a fraction of it and are unaffected.

qwen38._cap: no provider honours reasoning.max_tokens for this model. An earlier reading said Chutes did, on a probe that asked for 512 and got 462 -- the model simply thinks about that much unprompted. Asking for 64 returns 345.
qwen38._provider_choice: Venice, 2.5s against Chutes' 12.8s on the same probe. Chutes was chosen when the cap was believed to bind there; once it did not, speed was the only argument left.
qwen38._reasoning_headroom_why: Measured, not assumed. On a hard ProofNet row under the cell's own goedel_v1 prompt this model spends 25,566 reasoning tokens before it writes anything and still returns no content, ending in a provider error. The former 8192 cut it off mid-thought: the reply came back with finish_reason=length, zero characters of content, and the episode was filed as `no_code` -- the model failing to produce Lean, when in fact it never got to write any. Across the first 44 episodes of the four-cell control that was 37% of all attempts. 32,768 is the measured figure with headroom to spare; easy miniF2F rows cost a fraction of it and are unaffected.
qwen38._concurrency_why:
8, arrived at from both directions. The original 4 was set from 429s seen at concurrency 1 before the transport retried anything, and was over-cautious once backoff and Retry-After were in place. 16 was too far the other way: Venice returned 429s that survived three retries and three episodes were lost to it. 8 with six retries keeps the backoff ladder long enough (5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160s) to outlast a rate-limit window.

Speed here is not the provider's doing. Venice is the fastest of six endpoints benchmarked for this model (82 tok/s against 30-53), and the cell is slow because a dense 27B costs about nine times the compute per token of a 3B-active MoE, and this model also thinks the most in the panel at 29,873 reasoning tokens an episode.
qwen38._withdrawn:
Withdrawn from the panel. The group keeps two dense entries -- Muse-Glimmer-30B and Qwen3-14B -- and this was the third. Its control arm is complete (300/300, 30.0% miniF2F and 24.0% ProofNet, 103 claimed proofs re-verified) and is kept under qwen38_control for the record, but it is not reported.

One thing about it stayed unexplained and is recorded rather than smoothed over: 72% of its attempts produced no extractable Lean, against 10-13% for every other SLM once headroom was sized properly. Probed directly on an easy miniF2F row it emitted a clean fenced proof three times out of three, so the cell's rate is not a property the probe reproduces. The `no_code` branch was also the one attempt outcome that never recorded `truncated`, so the records cannot settle it either; that gap is now fixed for future runs.

qwen36._cap: no provider honours the cap for this model (64 requested: Venice 247, DeepInfra 417, SiliconFlow 434); headroom only
qwen36._provider_choice: Venice is the fastest fp8 endpoint for it by a wide margin -- 3.0s against DeepInfra's 18.6s and SiliconFlow's 11.9s on the same probe. Over 1905 episodes that ratio is the run.
qwen36._reasoning_headroom_why: Measured, not assumed. On a hard ProofNet row under the cell's own goedel_v1 prompt this model spends 15,879 reasoning tokens before it writes anything, finishing on its own. The former 8192 cut it off mid-thought: the reply came back with finish_reason=length, zero characters of content, and the episode was filed as `no_code` -- the model failing to produce Lean, when in fact it never got to write any. Across the first 44 episodes of the four-cell control that was 37% of all attempts. 24,576 is the measured figure with headroom to spare; easy miniF2F rows cost a fraction of it and are unaffected.

gptoss._model: openai/gpt-oss-20b, Apache-2.0, 21B total with 3.6B active -- a third mixture-of-experts entry, at the same active scale as nemotron and qwen3.6
gptoss._reasoning_headroom_why: Measured on three rows: 987 / 4,531 / 5,950 reasoning tokens, each finishing on its own with an extractable block. 12288 is about twice the largest observed, which is the margin the reasoning SLMs needed once ProofNet rows started running long.
gptoss._episode_concurrency_why: Lowered from 16 on 2026-09-04: DeepInfra rate-limits this model, and at 16 concurrent episodes 46 treatment episodes were cut short by HTTP 429 after six retries, then 7 more on the replay. The rate limit is a property of the host, so it is recorded here rather than worked around per run.

qwen3_14b._model: Qwen3-14B, a dense 14.8B model -- the third dense entry, and the one closest in scale to the Lean provers themselves (BFS 7B, Goedel 8B, Pythagoras 4B), so the group now spans a size-matched comparison as well as an architectural one.
qwen3_14b._provider_why: DeepInfra is the only endpoint for this model that declares a quantisation at or above eight bits: NextBit serves int4 and Alibaba reports `unknown`. The same check disqualified qwen3-8b outright, whose single endpoint declares nothing.
qwen3_14b._reasoning_headroom_why: Probed at 16384 and both an easy miniF2F row and a mid ProofNet row finished on their own with an extractable block, spending 4,679 and 4,160 reasoning tokens. 24576 leaves room for the harder rows, where every other SLM in the panel needed several times its easy-row figure. Reasoning is reported separately by this endpoint, so the proof budget binds exactly.
qwen3_14b._generate_timeout_why: The default is lean_timeout*2 = 360s. Probed on five rows this model finished in 48-242s on four of them and passed 1500s on the fifth, and that was a single request with nothing else in flight; at concurrency 12 the tail gets longer, not shorter. A request cut at 360s comes back with no attempts and is recorded as the model failing to prove the row. 900 clears the observed range, and waiting costs nothing that is measured -- the budget is tokens.
qwen3_14b._probe: Five rows at headroom 16384: four finished on their own with an extractable fenced block (6,779 / 4,451 / 2,582 / 13,743 completion tokens; reasoning 4,679 / 4,160 / 2,191 / 11,425), the fifth exceeded the probe's own 1500s client timeout. Reasoning is reported separately, so the proof budget binds exactly. Contrast qwen3.5-9b, tried for the same slot and rejected: at a 36,864-token ceiling it ran past the cap on four of six rows, spending up to 34,195 tokens on reasoning and returning no code at all -- on exactly the hard ProofNet rows the panel is there to measure.

muse_spark._model: meta/muse-spark-1.2, served by Meta through OpenRouter's contributor tier.
muse_spark._provider_why: No `provider` pin: Meta serves its own weights and the slug resolves to one endpoint. Same reasoning as nemotron_ultra.
muse_spark._quantisation: Meta declares none; single owner-operated endpoint, as above.
muse_spark._budget_binds: The contributor tier is the reason this cell is runnable. On the regular tier the model spent its whole completion allowance on reasoning and returned an empty body on hard ProofNet rows; raising the headroom would have fixed it at $4.25/M. Contributor is $0.20/M, so the headroom is set to 32768 without that cost.
muse_spark._contamination: Contributor routing shares prompts and completions with Meta. This does not touch what we measure -- the weights were frozen before we sent anything -- but it does mean this corpus may enter later Muse training, so a future Muse model cannot be a clean test of it.

nemotron_nano_9b._cap: Crusoe ignores the cap (512 requested, 1091 spent); headroom only
nemotron_nano_9b._model: NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2, dense 9B, the third dense entry and the one closest to the Lean provers in scale (BFS 7B, Goedel 8B). Its MoE sibling nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b is already in the group, so the pair is a same-family dense/sparse contrast with the training recipe held fixed.
nemotron_nano_9b._provider_why: Nvidia's own endpoint, and it declares bf16 rather than leaving it unstated -- which is what separates it from nemotron-3-ultra's `:free` slug and from qwen3-8b, both of which declare nothing. Free at the point of use.
nemotron_nano_9b._probe: Three rows at headroom 24576: 4,684 / 1,712 / 12,495 completion tokens (reasoning 2,811 / 1,469 / 9,814), every one finishing on its own with an extractable block. Reasoning is reported separately, so the proof budget binds. Slow at 31-42 tok/s, which the concurrency absorbs.
nemotron_nano_9b._first_party_why: NVIDIA's own NIM endpoint serving NVIDIA's own weights. The OpenRouter listing this cell first pointed at disappeared from the catalogue within the hour; this route is the maker's.
nemotron_nano_9b._serving: integrate.api.nvidia.com. The thinking arrives as `message.reasoning_content` rather than in `usage.completion_tokens_details`, which the transport now reads -- without it every thought would be charged against the proof budget.
nemotron_nano_9b._deadline: NVIDIA lists this API as deprecated after 2026-08-25, so the control arm is run now and the cell is expected to become unrunnable rather than merely slow.

inkling._cap: Crusoe ignores the cap (512 requested, 1091 spent); headroom only
inkling.quantization_exception: Served at nvfp4, below the panel's eight-bit floor. The free slug is the only Thinking Machines endpoint and it serves at four bits; the fp8 hosts are third-party and paid at $4.05/M, which puts a treatment arm out of reach. Reported at four bits rather than dropped, and read as a lower bound on the model rather than as a measurement of the released weights.
inkling._model: Inkling, open-weight MoE, 975B total and 41B active, from Thinking Machines Lab.
inkling._provider_why: Pinned to the maker's endpoint with fallbacks off, so the four bits are the four bits we report and not a route that may change.
inkling._withdrawn: Not run. `thinkingmachines/inkling:free` answers 403 to an ordinary chat completion --- `only available on agentic harnesses` --- so the free slug cannot be driven the way every other cell in the panel is. Routing it through an agent loop instead would not be the same measurement: the panel's fourteen other cells write a proof into a text box under a token budget, and an agent that plans and calls tools is a different protocol, which is exactly the confound that made the earlier codex-driven cell unusable. The fp8 hosts are third-party and paid at $4.05/M; a control arm there is about $25 and a treatment arm out of reach on the present budget.

gemini_flash._first_party_why: Google serving Google's own model; there is no third-party host and nothing to pin.
gemini_flash._serving: Vertex speaks its own protocol, so this cell uses the `genai` player rather than the OpenAI-compatible transport. Thinking arrives as `thoughts_token_count`, separate from `candidates_token_count`, which is what lets the proof budget charge the proof alone. Google bills thinking at the output rate regardless, so the invoice and the budget count different things here by design.
gemini_flash._probe: Three rows: 159 / 115 / 252 content tokens against 1,128 / 217 / 2,897 thinking, every one finishing on its own with an extractable block. The lightest content footprint in the panel -- Luna 945, grok 1,675, muse-spark 1,906 proof tokens an episode.
gemini_flash._generate_timeout_why: The genai adapter calls the SDK through asyncio.to_thread, which has no timeout of its own. Without one the cell stalled for 69 minutes on a single request: the process was alive, the episode file untouched, and nothing in the log said why. 600s covers the slowest observed episode with room, and the retry ladder handles the rest.

release307.note: 309 admitted release rows minus 2 the exam environment cannot elaborate.

release415.note: 417 released rows minus 2 the exam environment cannot elaborate. The arm the paper reports.

release535.note: The 535 rows the paper reports: the 537 admitted rows minus the 2 the exam environment cannot elaborate. Supersedes release415, which was the same corpus before 120 rows were added; a cell built on the older file resumes onto this one without replaying anything.

_report_split_by_benchmark: Never report one number over both benchmarks. The control is 50/50 and the
release is 169/138, so a combined figure compares weighted averages of
differently-composed sets. On the seeds BFS solves 28% of ProofNet and 60%
of miniF2F — the benchmark gap is larger than any effect being measured.
_local_control_environment: Every local cell runs on the same stack, because anything that differs
between two models is inside the number that separates them.
runtime      llama.cpp (Metal), one server at a time on this box
quantisation Q8_0 for all five local models
sampling     temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, declared per cell below
Quantisation is the one that was wrong. The three provers were Q8_0 while
Qwen3.6 ran Q4_K_M and gemma-4-12B ran Q4_0, so a general model scoring
below a prover would have been partly a statement about its quantisation.
Both general models were replaced with Q8_0 builds of newer checkpoints.
MLX is faster on this hardware and is deliberately not used: switching only
the new cells to it would reintroduce exactly the split this section removes,
and switching all of them means re-running three finished models.
Prompt dialect is the one thing that does vary, by design -- each model is
driven in its own official format, which is the protocol the paper states.
_two_comparison_groups: The panel is two groups, and a figure is read inside its group.
provers    bfs, goedel, pythagoras -- local, llama.cpp, Q8_0, ctx 16384.
The two whole-proof provers open their turn with the code
fence, which is the convention for the class and is available
to all of them because they are all served locally.
general    qwen, gemma, grok, luna -- hosted, no prefill. Not a choice:
+ frontier the assistant-turn prefill is not honoured by these endpoints,
measured on OpenRouter's Chutes and DeepInfra. Small open models
are therefore compared against frontier models through exactly
the same pipeline, which is the comparison that group is for.
Grouping this way keeps prefill from tracking the prover/general boundary.
Given to the provers only in one flat panel, 'the provers score higher' and
'the provers got the prefill' would not be separable.
_what_the_budget_counts: The budget is the proof the model writes: completion tokens minus reasoning
tokens. Thinking is generated, but charging it would hand a model that
deliberates for four thousand tokens less proof to write than one that
answers directly, on the same nominal budget.
It is also the only definition that means the same thing across the panel.
Measured: xAI caps `max_tokens` against the visible content and lets thinking
run past it (max_tokens 200 -> content exactly 200, reasoning 950 on top),
while Chutes caps the total (max_tokens 200 -> reasoning 200, content 0).
A total-token budget would have been two different quantities.
The three provers are unaffected: bfs, goedel and pythagoras emit no
reasoning channel at all, so content tokens are their completion tokens and
the finished cells stay valid. Only the reasoning models are re-accounted,
and none of them had a completed cell.
Attempts at capping the thinking itself were tried and do not work:
`reasoning.max_tokens` is ignored by xAI (64 requested, 289 spent),
is a hint that halves it rather than a ceiling.
_per_attempt_proof_allowance: Every whole-proof cell writes at most 4096 tokens of proof per attempt, four
attempts, inside a total budget of 8192 proof tokens.
`max_tokens` is that allowance. `reasoning_headroom` is what has to be added to
the *request*, because some endpoints count thinking inside the same cap: a
bare 4096 there leaves a few dozen tokens of Lean once thinking has run.
headroom 0     grok (xAI caps the visible answer), and the provers, which
emit no reasoning channel at all. Requesting 4096 delivers it.
headroom 8192  every reasoning SLM. Verified: qwen3.6 at Venice writes 809
proof tokens without it and 1420 with it, both finishing on

_groups_why: The panel reads in three groups, and the tables are grouped the same way.
lean_provers    trained on Lean proof data. bfs is the only tactic-step
model; the other three emit whole proofs and open their
reasoning_slms  small open models with no Lean-specific training. All four
emit a reasoning channel with no parameter asked for --
measured, not assumed -- which is why the group is named
for that rather than for being general-purpose. Balanced
two dense against two sparse so a difference between them
frontier_llms   neither interface enforces a token cap, so their absolute
scores are not comparable and only their drop is.
_treatments_why: The three finished cells keep the directory names they were run under.
Renaming them would strand 1245 measured episodes each: `--resume` keys on
(seed, attempt) inside the output directory, so a cell that cannot find its
own history replays the whole corpus. The names are stale --- they say 309
for a corpus that is now 535 --- and that is the cheaper of the two costs.
_parity_gate_gap: The budget gate compares a cell against its control and skips the check when
the control has no episodes yet. Launching control and treatment in one
invocation therefore starts the treatment before there is anything to compare
it against: leanstral's treatment ran 546 episodes with a prefill and no
reasoning while its control was later re-run without the prefill and with
reasoning on, and nothing objected. Run the control to completion first, or
the gate has nothing to hold.

Memory belongs to the REPL pool, which is sized separately: see `_lean_repl_pool_sizing`.
_lean_repl_pool_sizing: LEAN_REPL_POOL_SIZE is per *process*, and a panel runs one process per cell, so the
machine sees concurrency x cells REPLs. Setting it to 6 with five cells up put 30 Lean
processes on a 48 GB machine at 1.5-2.4 GB each; free memory fell to a third and the
kernel had paged out 408k pages. Measured: 1.6 GB per REPL.
Budget the total, not the per-cell number. A REPL is held only for the length of one
`verify` call, while an episode spends most of its wall clock waiting on the generator,
so a pool far smaller than the episode concurrency does not throttle it -- verification
queues briefly and generation keeps going. Twelve REPLs (~19 GB) across the panel leaves
the machine room to work; the run script exports it per cell rather than globally.
_retry_sizing: Six retries, not three. Three was enough for a rate limit but not for a dropped connection:
nemotron and qwen36 both aborted mid-treatment on three consecutive empties, and the errors
underneath were `Server disconnected without sending a response` and `no response` rather
than 429s -- twelve and eight episodes lost between them. A disconnect is the transport
giving up on a long generation, and these cells routinely spend ten minutes on one episode,
so the backoff ladder has to outlast a provider hiccup: 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160s.
